predictions.experiment: Wait-rate-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base and RL plain endpoints
predictions.recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T2 (RL plain) = s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl; T3 (base plain) = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. Use all rows of each file (500 each, cap hits included, no filtering; if a problem_index occurs twice keep the first row; missing rows are simply absent). For each row, rate = 1000 * (number of matches of the case-sensitive regex \bWait\b in the field text) / max(n_new, 1). Let m = median of the T2 rates (numpy.median). F_X = fraction of rows of file X with rate >= m (ties at m count as >=). Compute F_theta, F_T2, F_T3. Statistic S = (F_theta - F_T3) / (F_T2 - F_T3). Report S to 3 decimals.
predictions.note: Files: runs/theory-tests/abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl (theta0.25_plain, Modal), runs/theory-tests/s3/T2.jsonl and s3/T3.jsonl (S3 r4). Each file has 500 rows; first row per problem_index is kept; rate = 1000 * count of \bWait\b in text / max(n_new, 1). The median comes from statistics.median, which gives the same result as numpy.median. Ambiguity: ties at m. If many T2 rates are 0, the median m may be 0, and then every row satisfies rate >= m and all F values equal 1. alt_measured uses strict rate > m (ties excluded). If F_T2 = F_T3, S is undefined; the recipe does not call that refuted, so the script reports not_computable. Empty texts (n_new = 0) have rate 0. The theta prompt (180 tokens) differs from the T2/T3 prompt (96 tokens), but both are plain.

predictions.experiment: Answer-format-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base
predictions.recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T3 = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. All rows, cap hits included; first row per problem_index. A row is an 'answer-line' row if its text field contains no occurrence of the substring \boxed AND at least one line of the text, after stripping leading whitespace and any leading '*' or '#' characters, starts with the case-sensitive string 'Answer:'. s_X = (answer-line rows of X) / (rows of X). Statistic P = 1 - s_theta / s_T3. If s_T3 < 0.05 the statistic is undefined.
predictions.refuted_by: P below 0.60 or above 0.92, or undefined
predictions.note: Files: theta0.25_plain answers.jsonl and runs/theory-tests/s3/T3.jsonl. '\boxed' is matched as a literal backslash followed by 'boxed'. Main reading: for each line, strip leading whitespace, then any leading '*'/'#', then check startswith('Answer:') (case-sensitive). Other reading (alt_measured): strip whitespace, '*' and '#' together in any order, so '## **Answer:' also counts. If s_T3 < 0.05, the script reports measured null with refuted_by_met true, as refuted_by says. If s_T3 is below 0.05 under the main reading only, alt may still have a number. Lines such as 'Final Answer:' or 'answer:' do not count.

predictions.experiment: Accuracy of theta0.25_plain boxed answers against RL plain on the same problems
predictions.recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl (field score_v3); studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (field t2_right, grader v3, keyed by problem_index). Keep theta rows whose text contains the substring \boxed (cap hits included if they contain it; first row per problem_index). Drop rows whose problem_index has no entry in per_problem.json. For each kept row d = score_v3 (as 0/1; missing or null score_v3 counts as 0) - t2_right (as 0/1). Statistic D = mean of d over kept rows.
predictions.note: Files: theta0.25_plain answers.jsonl (score_v3) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (a list of dicts with problem_index and t2_right). Main reading: rows whose text contains the literal '\boxed' anywhere, including cap hits and boxed text that is not the final answer. A null or missing score_v3 counts as 0. Other reading (alt_measured): rows whose grader-v3 mode_v3 == 'boxed', meaning the final extracted answer is boxed. t2_right comes from the T2 RL plain run, a different sample from the theta run, so per-problem noise remains. If no row is kept, the script reports not_computable, because the recipe does not call that refuted.
